newsitem.title: BRAZIL: HSBC paid cash for Brazil's Bamerindus.
newsitem.headline: HSBC paid cash for Brazil's Bamerindus.

text.p: HSBC Holdings Plc paid $930 million in cash to take over healthy assets of Brazil's Bamerindus and set up Banco HSBC Bamerindus SA, said Altamir Lopes, head of the Central Bank's economics department.
Lopes, denying market speculation that the capital injection into the new bank may have been made through a Brady swap, said the cash entered into foreign reserves in March.
"They paid cash. The money entered into the reserves," he told Reuters.
In March, the Central Bank bought net $1.236 billion in the commercial dollar market, including the $930 million from HSBC, and sold $1.027 billion in the floating market, Lopes said.
The resulting $209 million surplus was converted into net reductions in foreign reserves of $404 million after $613 million was paid out.

Of that, $83 million covered obligations to the Paris Club of creditor nations and the rest payments to other international organizations and transactions under Reciprocal Trade Credits (CCRs), Lopes said.
Brazil's foreign reserves stood at $58.12 billion in March down slightly from $58.524 billion the month before.
According to the international liquidity concept, which includes accounts receivable, the reserves were $58.98 billion in March, down from $59.405 billion in February.

HSBC bought out ailing Bamerindus bank at the end of March. Critics claimed the London-based financial giant had got a cheap deal because it was using the face value of Bradies to pay. It was not immediately clear from Central Bank figures issued Monday whether HSBC had paid cash.
